access_limit: The public status report does not disclose the upstream evidence, classification state, rule evaluation or enforcement-control implementation that caused the incorrect suspensions.
The source was reviewed as external corroboration and does not independently establish every underlying claim.
The source does not determine legal liability or final factual truth.
Individual allegations and public replies do not establish private account facts or a common occurrence cause.

occurrence_evidence.claim: On 5 June, OpenAI investigated account-access problems at 13:26 and identified the issue at 14:20. At 15:19 it said some accounts had been incorrectly suspended and restoration was underway.
OpenAI marked services recovered at 16:09, then returned to monitoring at 19:09. Access was restored while subscription and credit work continued.

Subscription and credit remediation continued at 19:47. At 20:53 the provider said impacted users should have received email; at 21:19 it identified additional impacted users and promised further email.
At 06:16 on 6 June, OpenAI reported restored access and account/subscription email for incorrectly suspended users. The page gives no timezone.

A 9 June community author alleged a later ban, unanswered appeal and business disruption, and attributed it to the earlier error. No provider confirmation links that individual ban to this occurrence.

In a later community thread, users alleged continuing bans and appeal delays from late June into July and linked them to the June incident. Support requested a case number and later directed account-specific appeals to private channels. It did not confirm the claimed common cause.

criterion_tests.literal: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: Provider restoration and subscription credits support a corrected access disruption; later forum accounts do not establish a shared continuing outage. The shortfall relative to a governed threshold cannot be determined without the missing obligation.

criterion_tests.literal: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
criterion_tests.reason: The required response for this service cannot be inferred from the observed disruption: A binding account-specific continuity or reinstatement threshold at the suspension time.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

criterion_tests.literal: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
criterion_tests.reason: Interference or distress is preserved, but impairment of specifically obligated use is not established: Provider restoration and subscription credits support a corrected access disruption; later forum accounts do not establish a shared continuing outage.

criterion_tests.literal: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
criterion_tests.reason: The occurrence may engage continuity, but its independent obligation is unestablished: A binding account-specific continuity or reinstatement threshold at the suspension time.

criterion_tests.literal: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
criterion_tests.reason: Adequacy of an authorised response must be compared with that obligation; the observed response is: Provider restoration and subscription credits support a corrected access disruption; later forum accounts do not establish a shared continuing outage.

criterion_tests.literal: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
criterion_tests.reason: No measured satisfaction of the required service level follows from the available endpoint or recovery report: A binding account-specific continuity or reinstatement threshold at the suspension time.

criterion_tests.literal: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
criterion_tests.reason: This is an evidence-state exclusion, not proof that no duty existed. A binding account-specific continuity or reinstatement threshold at the suspension time.

criterion_tests.literal: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate concerns service operation or withdrawal, rather than a single inaccurate output: OpenAI false suspensions.

criterion_tests.literal: A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.
criterion_tests.reason: The validity, proportionality and sufficient alternatives of the restriction/response must be evidenced separately; A binding account-specific continuity or reinstatement threshold at the suspension time.

criterion_tests.literal: A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
criterion_tests.reason: Recovery adequacy or absence of a feasible required response is not established merely by eventual resolution: Provider restoration and subscription credits support a corrected access disruption; later forum accounts do not establish a shared continuing outage.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate includes an actual function/access question, not only its description: OpenAI false suspensions.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not confined to otherwise-valid access lost through identity or licence verification: OpenAI false suspensions.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
criterion_tests.reason: The candidate is not solely durable or restored work-state loss: OpenAI false suspensions.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
criterion_tests.reason: No claim that an infrastructure concession was demanded is the basis of this availability candidate: OpenAI false suspensions.

criterion_tests.literal: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
criterion_tests.reason: The proposed property concerns service function rather than only an interaction-level vulnerability response: OpenAI false suspensions.
